Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The England Women players take the field. Followed by Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana who walk out to open for India Women. It will be Katherine Brunt to start with the new ball. Will she be able to get an early breakthrough for her side?
... The Run Chase ...

Right then. India Women would certainly back themselves to chase this target down. England bowlers need to be disciplined here and a few early strikes will get them back in the game. Do join us for the chase shortly.

Shikha Pandey is in for a quick chat. She says that it was a dream to watch Renuka as she takes her five-wicket haul. Adds that the total is reachable with the batting lineup that they have. Ends by saying that they will give their best.

India Women were ruthless with the new ball, especially Renuka Singh. She ended her spell with a fi-fer and undoubtedly she stood out with the ball here. The Indian spinners could not quite put the batters under pressure in the middle overs. Shikha Pandey and Deepti Sharma took a wicket each.

England Women were in all sort of trouble when they were teetering at 29/3 at one stage. Natalie Sciver and Heather Knight consolidated really well. They soaked in all the pressure and accelerated really well in the middle over. Natalie Sciver went on to make her 50. She was exceptional with here reverse-hits but in the end, she got dismissed playing her most favourite stroke itself. Amy Jones; knock down the order could prove to be costly for India if they are unable to get off to a solid start with the bat.

England Women have scored 47 runs in the last 5 overs to get a competitive total on the scoreboard. Although, all the eyes are on Renuka Singh here as she walks out of the field with a fi-fer in a T20 World Cup. She certainly made the most of the cloud cover over her head.

FOUR BYES! A yorker and outside off, Sarah Glenn looks to guide it but misses. Richa Ghosh fails to grab it as well as the ball races away from the third man fence for a boundary. England Women end their innings for 151/7.
Sarah Glenn walks out to face the final delivery.

OUT! TAKEN! Two in two for Renuka Singh. Fuller and outside off, Katherine Brunt gets on her knee to slog it but gets the toe end of her bat. It carries towards long on and Radha Yadav settles under it to take a sitter. Katherine Brunt walks back for a golden duck and Renuka Singh is on a hat-trick now!
Commentary.Howout: c Radha Yadav b Renuka Singh

Commentary.Commentary: Katherine Brunt is the new batter.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Fuller and on middle and leg, Amy Jones shuffles across to scoop it but mistimes it completely. It lobs behind the sticks towards Richa Ghosh who pouches it comfortably. Amy Jones walks back after a fine knock!
Commentary.Howout: c Richa Ghosh b Renuka Singh

Commentary.Commentary: Too full, outside off, Sophie Ecclestone drives it towards covers for one.
Bowls it on off, Amy Jones scoops it towards fine leg for one again.
On a length and on off, Sophie Ecclestone taps it to covers for one.
SIX! Up and over. Fuller and outside off, Amy Jones pulls it over deep mid-wicket. Jemimah Rodrigues in the deep just gets her finger tips on it as it sails over the fence. Maximum!
Wide! Lands it wide outside off, Amy Jones offers no shot.
Bowls it outside off, Sophie Ecclestone cuts it towards point for one.
SIX! All the way. Fuller and outside off, Sophie Ecclestone moves forward and heaves it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum!
Bowls it on off, Amy Jones punches it towards mid off for one.
Another fuller one, Sophie Ecclestone drills it towards long on for one.
Fuller and outside off, Amy Jones slogs it towards mid-wicket for one.
Lands it down leg, Amy Jones misses her flick as the ball brushes her pads and rolls towards fine leg. They cross.
Fuller and outside off, Amy Jones chips it just over Harmanpreet Kaur at covers for a brace.
Lands it on off, Sophie Ecclestone taps it to mid off for one.
Bowls it on off, Sophie Ecclestone looks to flick it but gets an inside edge towards the left of the keeper. Close!
Fuller again, this is flicked towards mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller and on off, Amy Jones flicks it to deep id-wicket for a brace.
Fuller and outside off, Sophie Ecclestone eases it to covers.

OUT! TAKEN! Lands it outside off, Natalie Sciver looks to reverse sweep it but doesn't connect it well. It carries towards Smriti Mandhana at short third man. She takes a good catch diving forward. Natalie Sciver makes her way back into the hut after an excellent knock!
Commentary.Howout: c Smriti Mandhana b Deepti Sharma

Commentary.Commentary: Sophie Ecclestone is the new batter in.
Wide! This one lands wide outside off, Natalie Sciver offers no shot.
Another one outside off, Amy Jones cuts it towards point for one again.
Fifty up for Natalie Sciver. Fuller and outside off, Natalie Sciver sweeps it towards mid-wicket for one. What a knock!
Fuller and outside off, Natalie Sciver sweeps it but finds the fielder at square leg.
Flatter and outside off, Natalie Sciver looks to reverse sweep it but misses.
FOUR MORE! Excellent timing. Fuller and outside off, Amy Jones drives it uppishly, over covers for another boundary!
FOUR! Fine shot. Lands it on leg, Amy Jones gets on her knee and paddles it though fine leg as the ball races away from the fence for a boundary!
Another single as this is played toward mid-wicket.
Fuller again, this is driven towards mid off for one.
Lands it on middle, Natalie Sciver drills it to long off for one.
Fuller and on middle, Natalie Sciver eases it to the leg side.
SIX! Up, up and over. Fuller and on off, Amy Jones picks it well and slog sweeps it over deep mid-wicket as the ball sails into the stands!
Shorter and on off, Amy Jones ducks underneath it.
Bowls it on off, Natalie Sciver pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for one.
On a length and outside off, Natalie Sciver cuts it through point for a brace.
On a length and on off, Amy Jones drills it to long off for one.
FOUR! Cheeky from Amy Jones. Lands it outside off, Amy Jones shuffles across and scoops it through third man for a boundary!
Fuller and on off, Amy Jones pushes it to mid off for a quick single.

Fuller and outside off, it turns away a shade, Amy Jones looks to slog it but misses. Richa Ghosh collects it and whips off the bails. The umpires check for a possible stumping. The replay shows that she was well in. NOT OUT!
Fuller and on leg, Natalie Sciver tickles it to fine leg for one again.
Lands it on off, Amy Jones slogs it to mid-wicket for one.
A low full toss, on off, Natalie Sciver drives it to mid off for one.
Bowls it on middle, Natalie Sciver pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a brace.
On a length, outside off, Natalie Sciver drills it to long off for one.
Goes fuller again, Natalie Sciver eases it to the point fielder.
Fuller and on off, Amy Jones drives it to mid off for one.
On a length and on off, Amy Jones blocks it back. Three dots in a row.
Lands it down leg, Amy Jones misses her flick and gets rapped on her pads. Dot.
Fuller and outside off, Amy Jones defends it back.
Flighted up, on off, Amy Jones eases it to mid off for one again.
A low full toss, on off, Natalie Sciver flicks it towards mid-wicket for one.
Slightly shorter and on off, Amy Jones pulls it towards mid-wicket for one.
Slower one on off, Amy Jones taps it to the left of the bowler.
A low full toss, Natalie Sciver sweeps it towards backward square leg for one.
Fuller and on off, Natalie Sciver drives it to the woman at covers.

OUT! TAKEN! The partnership is finally broken. This one lands on off, slower too. Heather Knight looks to drive it but gets the upper part of her bat as it carries straight into the hands of Shafali Verma who pouches it with ease. Heather Knight walks back after a fine knock.
Commentary.Howout: c Shafali Verma b Shikha Pandey

Commentary.Commentary: Amy Jones walks in.
Wide! Lands it wide outside off, Heather Knight offers no stroke.
Another single as this is again played towards covers.
Fuller and outside off, Heather Knight drives it towards covers for one.
FOUR! Fine shot. Bowls it on middle, Heather Knight gets on her knee and slogs it over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Lands it outside off, Natalie Sciver cuts it to deep backward point for one.
Fuller and on off, Natalie Sciver eases it to mid off.

Drinks! India Women started off really well as Renuka Singh bagged three wickets inside powerplay and England Women were in a bit of trouble. The duo of Heather Knight and Natalie Sciver have steadied the sinking ship for them and stitched a partnership of 43 runs. They will hope to continue with their flurry of runs. India Women will look to break this stand soon.
A single to end as this is flicked to the leg side. 11 runs off this over. England Women are getting back in the game here.
FOUR! Natalie Sciver is finding the boundaries at will here. It is a full toss, on off. Natalie Sciver shuffles and swats it through mid-wicket for four more.
FOUR! Natalie Sciver moves to 30. It is full and on off. Natalie Sciver reverse-hits it fine, past the short third. The ball runs down to third man fence.
On middle and leg, tucked to the leg side for one more.
Very full, wide of off. Sciver comes across a long way and whips it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Flat and outside off. Sciver punches it to cover.
Short and on off. Sciver shuffles and tucks it to mid-wicket for a single. An expensive over by Rajeshwari Gayakwad comes to an end.
Loops it up, full and outside off. Heather Knight drives it through covers. The batters take three runs.
On off, tapped to point.
FOUR! Consecutive boundary. This is turning out to be a good phase for England. It is full, sliding down leg. Heather Knight sweeps it behind square on the leg side for four more.

FOUR! Top shot! This is a scoring stroke for Heather Knight. Once again the reverse sweep does the trick. It is full and outside off. Heather Knight reverse-sweeps it past backward point for four runs.
Short and on leg. Heather Knight goes back and works it to mid on.
Rajeshwari Gayakwad comes into the attack.
It is flatter and on fourth stump. Natalie Sciver mistime her reverse hit. 9 runs come off the over.
FOUR! Smacked! Back of a length, around off. Natalie Sciver siwvels and pulls it down to cow corner for a boundary.
It is full and on off. Knight works it o short third. The batters take a risky single. The replays confirm that Natalie Sciver is safe thanks to her desparate dive.
Floats it up, on leg. Heather Knight gets low and slogs it to deep mid-wicket. Once again lands short of the fielder. Two taken.
A single now as Natalie Sciver works it down to long on.
This is full and outside off. Heather Knight uses her feet and flicks it aerially to deep mid-wicket. It dies before reaching the fielder though. They take a single.
Full length, on off. Natalie Sciver shuffles across and scoops it over short fine leg. They take two before the fielder cuts it out.
Heather Knight moves outside off. The bowler follows her with a full one. Heather Knight carves it to deep point and takes a single.
Full, around off. Knight defends it out on her front foot.

Make that three! Fraction short, in the channel. Heather Knight dabs it down to short third man but finds the fielder. Richa Ghosh is close to the stumps restricting the batter to play from the crease.
Two dots to start with! Full this time, swinging in from outside off. Knight pushes it gently to the off side.
Length, on off. Knight hangs back and punches it to point.
Darted on the pads, Knight nudges it to deep square leg and takes a single. 8 runs off the over. England Women are 37/3 at the end of Powerplay here.
Too full and straight on the stumps. Natalie Sciver knocks it down to long on for a single.
Tossed up, full and outside off. Knight prods and paddles it towards short fine. One taken.

FOUR! Heather Knight adding salt to the wound here. It is full and on middle. Knight uses her feel and clips it past mid on. It races away to he fence as Shafali Verma is unable to get it under control at mid off.

A loud appeal for lbw but turned down! Deepti Sharma is interested and Harmanpreet Kaur goes for the review. Coming to the delivery - it is looped up, around off. It grips and turns in. Heather Knight prods and tries to go for the reverse-sweep but misses to take a hit on her pads. The UltraEdge confirms that Knight gets some glove on it. India Women lose another review here.
Natalie Sciver now rotates the strike as she pushes this full ball down the park.
Swing and a miss! It is a length ball, tailing into the pads. Knight takes a blow on her pads.
On a length, outside off. Heather Knight looks to chase it but gets beaten.
Heather Knight is the new batter.

OUT! TIMBER! Renuka Singh cannot do anything wrong here. The move to keep Renuka Singh has done wonders here for India Women. They will be delighted to see the back of Sophia Dunkley here. It is a full-length ball, on off, angled in. Sophia Dunkley makes some room and tries to punch it through the line but gets beaten. The ball goes through and uproots the leg pole. India Women back on top.
A length ball, on off. Natalie Sciver gets it to short fine off the inner half. They cross for one.
Short one, on off. Natalie Sciver pulls it to deep mid-wicket. They take two more runs.
A length ball, on leg. Sciver whips it past mid-wicket. The call is for two and they get two. India Women should try to save these runs here.
Natalie Sciver leans in and drives this full one to sweeper cover. One taken.

FOUR! EDGY! Natalie Sciver gets lucky this time. It is full, attacking the stump. Natalie Sciver tries to smack it through the line but gets an inside on it. The ball once again runs down to the fine leg fence. It does not really matter how the runs come now.
FOUR! Brave shot! It is full length, on off. Natalie Sciver shuffles and scoops it over the keeper's head. The ball races away to the fence.
Short and on off. Sciver pulls it hard but only to find the fielder at mid-wicket.
Length and on off. Sciver gets an inside edge to the leg side.
Full length, swinging away. Sophia Dunkley slashes hard at it. The ball catches the outside edge and flies to third man. One taken as there is protection in the deep.
Change. Pooja Vastrakar now comes into the attack.
Fuller, on off. Sophia Dunkley smacks it down to long by clearing her front leg. They take a single. Another successful over from Renuka Singh comes to an end.
In the air but safe! It is fuller, outside off. Sophia Dunkley ends up slicing it over covers. It evades the fielder and they take two runs.
It is full, wide of off. Sophia Dunkley shuffles across and long way. She tries to scoop it away but it comes off the cue-end.
Fuller, swinging in, on leg. Sciver wrists it to deep mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a single.

It is fuller, tailing into the pads. Natalie Sciver moves back and tries to flick it away but misses. She gets pinged on her pads. Renuka Singh appeals but the umpire is unmoved. Harmanpreet Kaur takes a review belatedly. The Ball Tracking confirms that the ball is missing the wicket. India Women lose a review here.
Natalie Sciver is the new batter in.

OUT! TIMBER! This is some masterclass inswing bowling. Renuka Singh gets her second wicket in no time. Singh dishes a full-length ball, around off. The ball lands and jags back in off the deck. Alice Capsey tries to be defensive but misses the line of the ball completely. She gets beaten on the inside edge and the ball sneaks through to hit the top of off. A dream wicket for any seamer.
Alice Capsey hangs back to this short one and cuts it hard to deep point. One taken. Relatively good over for England Women.
It is much fuller, outside off. Alice Capsey tries to smack it through the line but gets beaten by the away swing. Richa Ghosh though collects is well.
Full and on leg. Sophia Dunkley whips it through mid-wicket for a single.

Beaten! It is a length ball, on top of off. Sophia Dunkley comes down the track once again but is unable to put it away. Richa Ghosh now being asked to come closer to the stumps to keep Sophia Dunkley at home.
FOUR! Sophia Dunkley remains positive and gets the first boundary of the innings. It is pitched up, outside off. Sophia Dunkley uses her feet and crunches it past mid off. The ball races away.
Slightly short, outside off. Alice Capsey punches it to sweeper cover and crosses.
Shikha Pandey to share the new ball.
An inswinger, full and on off. Sophia Dunkley hangs back and dabs it to the off side. India Women right on top here.
A single now as this is worked down to long on.

Alice Capsey is cut in half this time. It is a length ball, that lands outside off and jags back in off the deck. Alice Capsey gets beaten on the inside edge but is fortunate to see the ball bounce over the stumps.
WIDE! Renuka Singh errs in her line this time and spills this full one down leg. Richa Ghosh does well to gather it.
Alice Capsey comes in at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Danni Wyatt has to head back to the dressing room on a golden duck. Richa Ghosh takes a stunning one-handed catch here. Renuka Singh angles in a length ball, around off. It lands and shapes away a touch. Danni Wyatt tries to be cheeky by playing it late but only gets a thick outside edge. The ball is flying away from the keeper, but Richa Ghosh dives to her right, with her right-arm fully strectched and pouches it safely.
Commentary.Howout: c Richa Ghosh b Renuka Singh

Commentary.Commentary: England Women and Sophia Dunkley are off the mark now. Fuller, on leg stump. Sophia Dunkley clips it down to long on and gets to the other end.
A length ball, angled into the pads. Sophia Dunkley shuffles and tries to flick it away but misses.

Done with all the pre-match proceedings. The India Women players are in a huddle near the ropes before they spread out on the field. Also, the opening pair of England Women - Sophia Dunkley and Danni Wyatt stride out to the middle. It will be Renuka Singh to start with the new ball, she will be looking for some swing early on. Here we go...

We are all set for the action but before that the two sides make their way out on the field and line-up for their respective national anthems. It will be India's first. Followed by England's anthem. It rained all day yesterday, there was some morning rain earlier, but thankfully, the conditions are much better now to play the game.
Pitch Report - Anjum Chopra is near the deck alongside WV Raman who stats that it is a new pitch. The surface looks nice and hard. The pacers would surely fancy themselves.

Heather Knight, the captain of England Women starts by saying that losing the toss is not a problem. Mentions that they are going unchanged. Adds the conditions are friendly for the spinners. Informs the batters need to assess the condition quickly and get into the game as soon as possible.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the skipper of India Women is in for a chat. She says that chasing would be a better option. Tells that they have one change, Devi comes in. Mentions their bowling has been a concern but would hope to stick to the plans. Adds that it is an important game.

England Women (Unchanged playing XI) - Sophia Dunkley, Danni Wyatt, Alice Capsey, Natalie Sciver, Heather Knight (C), Amy Jones (WK), Katherine Brunt, Sophie Ecclestone, Charlotte Dean, Sarah Glenn, Lauren Bell.

India Women (Playing XI) - Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Pooja Vastrakar, Radha Yadav, Rajeshwari Gayakwad, Renuka Singh, Shikha Pandey (Comes in for Devika Vaidya).
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of India Women. They will BOWL first.

England got off to a strong start in the tournament and has put on two outstanding all-around performances in the games they have played so far. They will look to carry on with the momentum and win this important game. Meanwhile, India's performances have been quite clinical. The Woman in blue will look to win this game and climb to the top spot of the points table. Which side will come out on top? Let's find out together. Toss and team news in a bit...

Hello and a warm welcome to all! It is now time for the 14th match of the Women's T20 World Cup as England Women take on the India Women at St George's Park, Gqeberha. Both sides started off their campaign well and won both of their matches comfortably. England Women have been ruthless and their NRR speaks for their dominance. Both sides will be hoping to win this game and stay on top of the table. Let's hope for a exciting game of cricket.
... MATCH DAY ...

The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2023 is finally up and running, and the stakes could not be higher. All teams have played at least two games and had time to assess the pitch and conditions. Each game from here can decide a team's fate when it comes to eventually winning the World Cup. After the semi-final exit in the last edition, England Women will be looking to go two better and win the tournament as they did in the first-ever edition. Not only do they have the team, but they also have the momentum, as they have won both of their games in the tournament so far. Sophie Ecclestone and Sarah Glenn have been exceptional with the ball, while Danni Wyatt and Alice Capsey will be key in scoring runs against a strong opponent this time around. Coming into this tournament, the expectations for the India Women's team were at an all-time high, and their performances so far have taken them even higher. With two wins in two games, Team India will want to remain undefeated and clinch the ICC T20 World Cup for the first time. They have probably the best batting, and their batters will look to continue the good form. Richa Ghosh has been brilliant for them, and in her, they have a perfect finisher. Deepti Sharma will look to provide another all-round performance to help her side to their third win. This match will be between two top teams, and as both sides will try to get the better of the other, we can expect a fiery contest. Let's see who comes out on top.
